To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the hyperpolarization evoked by calcium injection in hamster eggs was due to a calcium-dependent potassium conductance.
the recovery phase of calcium-evoked responses in hamster egg cells is slowed by the metabolic uncoupler, dinitrophenole, by quercetin, and by lanthanum.
the hyperpolarization produced by micro-injections of Ca2+ into the oocyte cytoplasm is due to the entry of Ca2+ through voltage-sensitive Ca2+ channels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of calcium micro-injection on electrical properties of the hamster egg.
the role of the extracellular medium in the regulation of the calcium-evolved responses of hamster eggs.
the effect of lanthanides on the intracellular calcium concentration and the role of calcium extrusion on the recovery phase from calcium-evoked responses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

calcium-evoked electrical potentials are due to an increase in membrane conductance to potassium, and that the recovery from the calcium-evoked hyperpolarization is slowed by extracellular lanthanides or quercetin, but is not slowed by dinitrophenal, suggesting a role for the plasma membrane calcium extrusion system in the recovery of the hyperpolarization.
lanthanum, dinitrophenols and quercetin all act to prolong the recovery phase of calcium-evoked hyperpolarizing responses.

the calcium-evoked hyperpolarizing responses in the eggs of the golden hamster are not mediated by a calcium-activated potassium channel, nor are they mediated by the calcium-dependent chloride conductance described in the mouse egg.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hyperpolarization produced by calcium injection results from an electrogenic calcium extrusion mechanism which has a reversal potential of about -80 mv.
the hyperpolarizations produced by calcium or strontion injections in hamster eggs are due to a calcium-activated chloride conductance.

the calcium-evoked hyperpolarizations are due to a calcium-dependent potassium conductance and that this conductance is controlled by a calcium extrusion process that is sensitive to both lanthanum and quercetin.
The main takeaway from our work is that

calcium entry into the cell is not the only factor that determines the time course of calcium-evoked responses and that the recovery phase of these responses is not necessarily a reflection of the activity of a calcium extrusion mechanism.
lanthanum and quercetin appear to block calcium extrusion from hamster eggs.
calcium-evoked electrical events are not due solely to the activation of a voltage-dependent calcium current, but are also dependent on the activity of a calcium extrusion pathway.
